chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When you enter the Haram, take from the Izkhir (fragrant grass) and chew it.
Al-Kulayni said, 'I asked one of our companions about this, so he said, 'It is recommended to do so to freshen the mouth with it for kissing the Stone'.

key_terms.الْإِذْخِر: A type of fragrant grass used for chewing to freshen breath
key_terms.الْحَرَم: The Sacred Precincts (specifically Mecca or Medina)
key_terms.تَقْبِيلِ الْحَجَر: Kissing the Stone (referring to the Black Stone in the Kaaba)
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: It is recommended (a category of fiqh ruling)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended practice for freshening breath before kissing the Black Stone in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi highlights the emphasis on physical purity and pleasantness (tayyib) in Shia devotional practices, linking bodily preparation to the reverence shown to sacred symbols. The scholarly explanation provided by Al-Kulayni clarifies that this act is not merely hygienic but serves to enhance the spiritual experience of kissing the Black Stone, reflecting the broader Islamic principle of presenting oneself in the best manner before God.
